overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Centre of Mass of a Rigid Body, Centre of Mass Motion, providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Centre of Mass of a Rigid Body, Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: A rigid body is a body with a perfectly fixed shape where relative distances between all constituent particles remain constant. General motion of a rigid body can be decomposed into translation of its centre of mass and rotation about the centre of mass.

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Centre of Mass of a Rigid Body, Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: In pure translational motion, all particles of a rigid body have identical velocities and accelerations at any given instant. In pure rotational motion about a fixed axis, all particles move in circles with the same angular velocity omega.

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Centre of Mass of a Rigid Body, Centre of Mass Motion
blocks.contentMarkdown: If a projectile explodes in mid-air, the centre of mass of its fragments continues along the original parabolic trajectory under gravity. When an explosion occurs in an airborne projectile, the fragment trajectories diverge due to internal forces, but the centre of mass of all fragments continues along the exact same parabolic trajectory determined solely by external gravitational force, until fragments hit the ground.
